outlook.statement: The Directors remain focused on restoration and optimization of operations, cost management, prudent working-capital management, strengthening governance and pursuing sustainable growth.

India's steel demand is projected to grow, fueled by infrastructure development and government initiatives. The National Steel Policy targets 300 million tonnes of steel-making capacity by 2030-31 and per-capita steel consumption to rise to 160 kg by 2030. The company's captive power capability and 40 MW power-generation infrastructure provide an operating advantage for energy-cost management.

Global overcapacity, trade distortions, economic uncertainties, volatility in sponge-iron and ferro-alloy prices, availability and pricing of key raw materials, coal and energy-price movements, foreign-exchange movements affecting imported inputs, environmental and regulatory requirements, and geopolitical tensions (US-Iran tensions, Strait of Hormuz disruption) pose challenges and may affect prices, demand, input logistics, and increase compliance and operating costs.

India GDP growth for FY 2025-26 was 7.7%. Expect India to grow between 6.4% and 6.6% in FY2026-27 and have a stronger outlook thereafter. If global uncertainties recede, growth may surpass 7% over the next two years. Baseline scenario expects India to grow between 7.1% and 7.6% during FY2026, followed by 6.6% and 7.7% over the next two years.

India's crude steel production projected to reach 255 million tonnes at 85% capacity utilisation achieving 230 million tonnes of finished steel production by 2030. Consumption expected to reach 206 million tonnes by 2030 with net exports of 24 million tonnes. Per-capita steel consumption anticipated to grow to 160 kg.

The domestic consumption is considered to move at a same momentum as is evident in the demand pull visible in infrastructure, automobile and other sectors. Government is also driving the economy by investing in housing, roads, and ports and in other infrastructure projects. Favorable domestic demand and remunerative prices in both domestic and international markets are likely to bolster steel production further in the years to come, resulting into more demand for sponge iron.

The Company's medium-to-long-term outlook is supported by expected growth in domestic steel consumption, infrastructure investment and manufacturing activity. The transition to the new management and the associated modification programme are important factors in the Company's near-term operating trajectory. Management's ability to restore and sustain production capacity, improve utilisation, manage raw-material and energy costs, strengthen working capital and realise the benefits of the new ownership structure will be key determinants of future performance.

The company expects to fully recover the carrying amounts of the assets and comfortably discharge its debts and obligations. Hence the management does not envisage any material impact on the audited financial statements of the company for the year ended on 31st March 2026.
